glance.summary: Anthropic has filed for an IPO, revealing growing revenue, rising losses, and heavy enterprise adoption.
Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to up to 60,000 employees across four countries.
OpenAI announced three science discoveries in math, computer science, and physics with academic guides.
SAP is letting professionals renew their certifications using AI-based roleplays.

big_pour.headline: Anthropic officially files for an IPO
big_pour.summary: Anthropic officially filed for an IPO, revealing soaring revenue alongside mounting losses. The filing also showed major enterprise adoption and an unusual governance structure built to preserve founder control and AI safety.
big_pour.why: It shows how an AI company balances rapid corporate growth, heavy financial losses, and safety missions.

explain.kid: A big AI company called Anthropic is getting ready to sell stock to the public. It is making much more money, but also losing more, while keeping special rules so its founders stay in control of safety.
explain.pm: Anthropic filed for an IPO, showing strong enterprise adoption and soaring revenue offset by mounting losses. Their unusual governance model aims to balance founder control with their AI safety mission as they scale.
explain.engineer: Anthropic’s IPO filing reveals soaring revenue and major enterprise adoption paired with mounting losses. The company is using an unusual governance structure to protect founder control and its core AI safety mission.

big_pour.headline: Microsoft offers buyouts to 60,000 employees
big_pour.summary: Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to up to 60,000 employees across the US, UK, Canada, and India. The program gives staff financial support and career planning resources as the company trims staff.

big_pour.headline: OpenAI announces three major science discoveries
big_pour.summary: OpenAI announced three major discoveries in math, computer science, and physics. The work relied on external academic experts, described as "shepherds", who guided the results.

office_blend.headline: Bayer Crop Science builds AI decision engine
office_blend.summary: Bayer Crop Science built a multi-agent platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. It allows breeders, analysts, and researchers to ask natural language questions about their analytics platform.

office_blend.headline: SAP updates certification renewal with AI roleplays
office_blend.summary: SAP professionals can now renew their certifications through AI-based roleplays. The service shifts focus from learning facts toward evaluating how people apply knowledge in real-world use cases.

still_roasting.summary: TechCrunch Founder Summit 2026 will explore customer acquisition, team building, pitch sharpening, founder leadership, and scaling companies inside and outside startup hubs.
NetSuite is launching SuiteExpress to connect into Customer Success services for ERP implementation and optimization.

quick_sips.summary: Apple released iOS and macOS 27.2 with new Siri AI features and options to limit direct application access.
The RealReal updated its bot defense system to make it harder for AI agents to shop on its website.
AI assistants answering junior engineers' foundational questions reduce Slack interruptions but risk eroding senior engineers' architectural fluency.

stories.label: New launch
stories.headline: OpenAI launches GPT-6.1 Terra
stories.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-6.1 Terra, cutting API prices in half and delivering major gains in coding and computer-use benchmarks. However, its safety report flagged a catch.

stories.label: New tool
stories.headline: Ex-GitHub CEO launches GitHub alternative
stories.summary: Thomas Dohmke, former GitHub CEO, launched Entire, a GitHub alternative that replaces traditional pull requests.

long_read.headline: What’s the ROI of software engineers’ spending on AI?
long_read.summary: The newsletter analyses data from 27 companies to see whether increased AI spending has changed shipping velocity and PR output for software engineers.

sign_off: That's the last sip. See you next morning.

word.definition: Making a model answer from specific provided sources (documents, search results, database rows) rather than from what it memorised in training.
word.heard: "Is that answer grounded, or is the model guessing?"
word.analogy: Like making a drink from the recipe card in front of you instead of from memory.

keep_brewing.name: One Useful Thing
keep_brewing.description: Ethan Mollick's newsletter on using AI at work, written for non-engineers.
